newsitem.title: USA: Shell Chemical to build U.S. CARILON plant.
newsitem.headline: Shell Chemical to build U.S. CARILON plant.

text.p: Shell Chemical Co said Wednesday it will build a U.S. facility to manufacture CARILON Polymers.

The company said a manufacturing plant for the new family of aliphatic polyketone engineering polymers will be built at its chemical complex in Geismar, La. Construction is slated to begin the third quarter of 1997, with startup anticipated in early 1999.
The Royal Dutch/Shell Group subsidiary declined to disclose the cost of the facility. A spokeswoman would only said "100s of millions of dollars."
CARILON Polymers were first introduced in Europe in 1995 and in the U.S. in 1996. They have have been manufactured commercially by Shell affiliate in Carrington, England, since October 1996.
The company said the new facility "will significantly increase" its total production capacity, but did not disclose its present capacity.

It did say the planned 87,500-square-foot plant will be constructed in two phases. Its initial annual capacity will be 55 million pounds (25 kilotons), with an expansion to 110 million pounds (50 kilotons) upon market demand.
